\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گزارش} (gozâresh)}{گزارش (gozâresh)}]{\fa{گزارش} (gozâresh) — a report}

\label{lesson:FA-C308-gozaresh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for the eve, then the Persian for roughly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گزارش}}
\textbf{\fa{گزارش}} (\emph{gozâresh}) — \textquotedblleft{}a report\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{گزارش} \fa{او} \fa{درباره} \fa{مدرسه} \fa{های} \fa{روستا} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Gozâresh-e u darbâre-ye madrese-hâ-ye rustâ bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Her report was about the village schools.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{gozâresh-hâ}. Built on \emph{gozâr-}, the stem of \emph{gozârdan} \textquotedblleft{}to set out, to render\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gozâresh} is a native Persian noun: the stem \emph{gozâr-} \textquotedblleft{}to set out, to render\textquotedblright{} with the noun suffix \emph{-esh}. EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gozâresh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gozâresh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{gozâresh}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for the eve, then the Persian for roughly, then say \emph{gozâresh} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گزارش} \fa{دادن} (gozâresh dâdan)}{گزارش دادن (gozâresh dâdan)}]{\fa{گزارش} \fa{دادن} (gozâresh dâdan) — to report}

\label{lesson:FA-C308-gozaresh-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for roughly, then the Persian for a report.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گزارش} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{گزارش} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{gozâresh dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to report\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{راننده} \fa{تصادف} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{پلیس} \fa{گزارش} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Rânande tasâdof râ be polis gozâresh dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The driver reported the crash to the police.
\end{quote}

Present stem \emph{dah-}: \emph{gozâresh midahad}. The thing reported takes \emph{râ}; the person told takes \emph{be}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gozâresh dâdan} joins the native noun \emph{gozâresh} \textquotedblleft{}a report\textquotedblright{} with \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB takes back to the Indo-European root \emph{deh\textsubscript{3}-}: to give a report.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gozâresh dâdan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{gozâresh dâdan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for roughly, then the Persian for a report, then say \emph{gozâresh dâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گزارشگر} (gozâreshgar)}{گزارشگر (gozâreshgar)}]{\fa{گزارشگر} (gozâreshgar) — a reporter, a correspondent}

\label{lesson:FA-C308-gozareshgar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a report, then the Persian for to report.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گزارشگر}}
\textbf{\fa{گزارشگر}} (\emph{gozâreshgar}) — \textquotedblleft{}a reporter, a correspondent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{گزارشگر} \fa{از} \fa{جلوی} \fa{بیمارستان} \fa{صحبت} \fa{میکرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Gozâreshgar az jelo-ye bimârestân sohbat mikard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The reporter was speaking from outside the hospital.
\end{quote}

\emph{-gar} makes a person who does something, as in \emph{kârgar} \textquotedblleft{}worker\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gozâreshgar} adds the native suffix \emph{-gar} \textquotedblleft{}one who does\textquotedblright{} to \emph{gozâresh} \textquotedblleft{}a report\textquotedblright{}. EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تیتر} (titr)}{تیتر (titr)}]{\fa{تیتر} (titr) — a headline}

\label{lesson:FA-C308-titr}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to report, then the Persian for a reporter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تیتر}}
\textbf{\fa{تیتر}} (\emph{titr}) — \textquotedblleft{}a headline\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{تیتر} \fa{روزنامه} \fa{امروز} \fa{خیلی} \fa{بزرگ} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Titr-e ruznâme-ye emruz kheyli bozorg bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Today's newspaper headline was very big.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{titr-hâ}. Also the title line of a television news item.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{titr} is usually traced to French \emph{titre}, \textquotedblleft{}title\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اخبار} (akhbâr)}{اخبار (akhbâr)}]{\fa{اخبار} (akhbâr) — the news (programme)}

\label{lesson:FA-C308-akhbar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a reporter, then the Persian for a headline.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اخبار}}
\textbf{\fa{اخبار}} (\emph{akhbâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}the news (programme)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدرم} \fa{هر} \fa{شب} \fa{ساعت} \fa{نه} \fa{اخبار} \fa{را} \fa{تماشا} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pedaram har shab sâ'at-e noh akhbâr râ tamâshâ mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father watches the news every night at nine.
\end{quote}

The Arabic broken plural of \emph{khabar} \textquotedblleft{}a piece of news\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Akhbâr} is the news in general or the news programme.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{akhbâr} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{akhbār} (EtymDB), the broken plural of \emph{khabar} \textquotedblleft{}news\textquotedblright{}, which Persian also has.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
